product.summary: For three cities, bus and tram departure times shown in a phone app

source.quote: NextStop is a phone app that shows bus and tram departures for three cities
We have run NextStop for six years.

evidence.value: 1.1 million monthly users, flat for two years

source.quote: It has 1.1 million monthly users and about 180,000 daily users, and these numbers have been flat for two years.

evidence.value: Ads bring in about $9,000 a month

source.quote: Ads bring in about $9,000 a month.
the backend is two small services and a cache, and it is boring on purpose

items.text: backend of two small services and a cache

source.quote: the backend is two small services and a cache
Ines writes the Swift and Kotlin apps
Rafael writes the Go backend

items.text: favourite stops kept on the phone, not on the servers

source.quote: Favourite stops are stored on the phone, not on our servers.

external_systems.name: the transit agencies' open data feeds
external_systems.role: source of departure times and delays, polled and cached by the backend

source.quote: departure times and delays come from the transit agencies' open data feeds

external_systems.role: serves the app's ads; receives the device's advertising identifier

It has 1.1 million monthly users
about 180,000 daily users

observed.what: transit feeds polled and cached; almost all traffic is reads

source.quote: Almost everything is reading: departure times and delays come from the transit agencies' open data feeds, which our backend polls every 30 seconds and caches.

projected.what: Ashford transit agency's conditional estimate if its invited city is added next year, not guaranteed or current traffic

source.quote: Ashford's transit agency has invited us to add their city next year, which they say would bring about 400,000 more monthly users.
On weekdays between 7am and 9am, and again between 4pm and 7pm, requests run at about 5 times the daily average.
On snow days we have seen 10 times the average for a whole morning.

targets.what: Riverton service alerts shown after publication

source.quote: requires us to show its service alerts within 2 minutes of publication

availability.value: Must work during rush hour; night outages go unnoticed

source.quote: During rush hour the app has to work: an outage at 8am means thousands of one-star reviews and angry emails to the agencies. At 2am nobody notices.

data_loss_tolerance.value: No user data to lose; everything can be fetched again from the feeds

source.quote: There is no user data to lose; everything we show can be fetched again from the feeds.

recovery_time.value: Night failures wait until morning (no on-call)

source.quote: We are not on call; if something breaks at night, it waits until morning.
We collect no names, emails or accounts.

data_categories.value: phone location, used on the phone only

source.quote: The app uses the phone's location to find nearby stops, and the location never leaves the phone
We keep anonymous usage counts for 90 days.

data_categories.value: device advertising identifier, passed to the ad network

source.quote: Our ad network receives the device's advertising identifier.

source.why: No accounts or names; location stays on the phone; only anonymous counts and an advertising identifier leave it.

unknowns.question: Will Ashford's feed allow polling every 30 seconds, and in what format is it?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Adding Ashford would add about 400,000 monthly users and a new feed; its limits and format decide the caching and ingestion design.

unknowns.question: Does the product need any security control beyond the usual for a public, read-only app?
unknowns.why_it_matters: The brief asks for none; there are no accounts and no user data on the servers, so no option turns on it.

unknowns.question: Has the product faced any named threat or abuse?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; the data served is public, so no option turns on it.

unknowns.question: Does any certification or audit apply?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named and no regulated data is held.

assumptions.text: Ashford's 400,000 users are a possible addition next year, not current load.
assumptions.why: The brief gives it as the agency's own estimate for a city not yet added.
